akhfash:4-4.t:
He said ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ﴾: its singular is "العُشَراء" (a she-camel ten months pregnant), like "النُفَسَاء" (a woman in childbed), with "النِفاس" for the plural. And the poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-eighth verse cited as evidence]:
رُبَّ شريبٍ لَك ذي حُساس * ريانَ يَمْشِي مِشْيَةَ النِّفَاسِ
(Many a drinking-companion of yours, keen of feeling, sated with drink, walks with the gait of women in childbed.)
And "النُّفاس" is also said.

akhfash:6-6.t: And some read ﴿سُجِرِّتْ﴾ (with doubling), and some read it light, citing as proof ﴿وَٱلْبَحْرِ ٱلْمَسْجُورِ﴾. The correct way is the doubling, because when that is "broken" it comes on this pattern: one says "قُطِّعُوا" and "قُبِّلوا", and one does not say of a single person "قُطِّعَ", meaning his hand, nor "قُتِّلَ". «[Translator's note: the source writes «كسر» ("broken") and «يقل»; presumably «كثر» ("multiplied") and «يقال» ("it is said") are meant: the doubled form is used for many subjects.]»

akhfash:8-9.t:
And He said ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ﴾: "وَأَدَهُ" "يَئِدُهُ" "وَأْداً" ("to bury alive"), like "وَعَدَهُ" "يَعِدُهُ" "وَعْداً", the ʿayn (middle radical) being in the manner of a hamza.
And He said ﴿سُئِلَتْ﴾ ﴿بِأَىِّ ذَنبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾; and some read ﴿سَأَلَتْ﴾ — she herself (asked).

akhfash:12-12.t: And He said ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ﴾ light, and some read it heavy (doubled), because its kindling was intensified against them. «[Translator's note: the source writes «جرّها»; presumably «حرّها», "its heat", is meant. The quotation in the source is printed with the doubled form.]»

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿ٱلْجَوَارِ ٱلْكُنَّسِ﴾: its singular is "كانِس", and [the plural]* is "كُنَّس", as you say "عاطِل" and "عُطَّل".

akhfash:24-24.t: And He said ﴿وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى ٱلْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ﴾: He means "that is: stingy" (ببخيل). And some read ﴿بِظَنين﴾, that is: suspected (متَّهَم), because some of the Arabs say "ظننت زيدا", so "هو ظنين", that is: I suspected him, so "he is suspected" (هو مُتَّهَم).

daas-irab:1-6.t: ﴿إِذَا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿الشَّمْسُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned after it; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿كُوِّرَتْ﴾: a passive past verb, its deputy agent being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is explicative and has no grammatical position. The verses following it are conjoined to it and their i'rab is the same.

daas-irab:7-9.t: The verse is conjoined to what precedes it, and the one following it is also conjoined. ﴿بِأَيِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) قتلت; ﴿ذَنْبٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿قُتِلَتْ﴾: a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of سئلت.

daas-irab:10-14.t: The four verses 10–13 are conjoined to what precedes them and their i'rab is clear. ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿ما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position; ﴿أَحْضَرَتْ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:15-22.t:
﴿فَلا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿لا﴾ is redundant (zāʾida); ﴿أُقْسِمُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِالْخُنَّسِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿الْجَوارِ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of الخنس; ﴿الْكُنَّسِ﴾: a second adjective. ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ﴾: conjoined to الخنس; ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿عَسْعَسَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).
﴿وَالصُّبْحِ إِذا تَنَفَّسَ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لَقَوْلُ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿قول﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the nominal clause is the answer to the oath; ﴿رَسُولٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿كَرِيمٍ﴾: adjective; ﴿ذِي﴾: a second adjective of رسول; ﴿قُوَّةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿عِنْدَ﴾: an adverb of place; ﴿ذِي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿الْعَرْشِ﴾: also muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿مَكِينٍ﴾: a third adjective of رسول; ﴿مُطاعٍ﴾: a fourth adjective; ﴿ثَمَّ﴾: an adverb of place meaning "there"; ﴿أَمِينٍ﴾: a fifth adjective of رسول. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿ما﴾ is negative, working like laysa; ﴿صاحِبُكُمْ﴾: its noun; ﴿بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾: genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ما.

daas-irab:23-26.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive, the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and ﴿قد﴾ is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿رَآهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position; ﴿بِالْأُفُقِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْمُبِينِ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of الأفق.
﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿وَما﴾: the Ḥijāzī negative mā; ﴿هُوَ﴾: its noun; ﴿عَلَى الْغَيْبِ﴾: attached to what follows them; ﴿بِضَنِينٍ﴾: genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿ما﴾ is Ḥijāzī; ﴿هُوَ﴾: its noun; ﴿بِقَوْلِ﴾: genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ما; ﴿شَيْطانٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿رَجِيمٍ﴾: adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَيْنَ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and ﴿أين﴾ is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as an adverb of place; ﴿تَذْهَبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:27-29.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾: negative; ﴿هُوَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿ذِكْرٌ﴾: khabar (predicate); ﴿لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾: badal (substitute) for His words للعالمين; ﴿شاءَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿أَنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, the agent being latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is the object of شاء. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿تَشاؤُنَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception; ﴿أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative by an, and the Name of Majesty is its agent; ﴿رَبُّ الْعالَمِينَ﴾: badal, muḍāf to العالمين; the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by annexation to an adverb of time, the implied form being: "وقت أن يشاء الله" (at the time that Allah wills).

farraa:1-1.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذَا ٱلشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾: its light is gone.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: [128/a] ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلنُّجُومُ ٱنكَدَرَتْ﴾.
That is: they scattered and fell on the face of the earth.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ﴾.
العشار: the pregnant she-camels; their owners abandon them, being occupied with themselves.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ Sallām ibn Sulaym narrated to me from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq from ʿIkrima, who said: their gathering is their death.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ﴾.
They opened into one another and became one sea.

farraa:7-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلنُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ Sallām ibn Sulaym narrated to me from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq Abū Sufyān from ʿIkrima, concerning His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلنُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ﴾. He said: the man is paired in Paradise with his righteous companion of this world, and the man who used to do evil deeds is paired in the Fire with his companion who used to help him in that; that is the pairing of the souls. Al-Farrāʾ said: I heard one of the Arabs say: زوّجت إبلي (I paired my camels); and Allah forbade pairing two together — that is, tying one camel to another so that they feed together and travel together.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from his father from Ibn ʿAbbās; and ʿAlī ibn Ghurāb narrated to me from Ibn Mujāhid from his father from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ بِأَىِّ ذَنبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, identical to the standard reading; Ibn ʿAbbās's reported reading is «سَأَلَتْ … قُتِلْتُ», which the following remarks presuppose], and he said: she is the one who asks and is not asked. It is also permissible to read: ﴿بِأىِّ ذَنبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾ with the meaning: for what sin was I killed (قُتِلْتُ), as you say in speech: ʿAbdullāh — for what sin was he beaten (ضُرِبَ), and: for what sin was I beaten (ضُرِبْتُ). Parallels to this from reported speech (ḥikāya) have already been mentioned; of that kind is [128/b] the saying of ʿAntara:
الشاتِمى عِرضى ولم أشتمها * والناذرين إذا لقيتهما دمى
(The two who revile my honour though I did not revile them, and who vowed my blood if I met them.)
The meaning is: the two of them used to say: "If we meet ʿAntara we will surely kill him." So the speech ran in his poem according to this meaning, while the wording differs. Likewise his saying:
رَجْلان من ضَبة أخبرانا * إنا رأينا رجلا عريانا
(Two men of Ḍabba informed us: "We saw a naked man.")
The meaning is: they informed us that they [had seen]; but it ran according to the manner of direct speech, as one says: ʿAbdullāh said: إنه لذاهب (he is going) and إني ذاهب (I am going), the going being his in both ways.
Whoever reads: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ﴾ has two interpretations in it. سُئلت: she was asked, and it was said to her: ﴿بِأَىِّ ذَنب قُتلتِ﴾ (for what sin were you killed?); then قُتلتْ is permissible, just as it was permissible in the first question. Or سُئلت may mean: those who buried her alive were asked about her, as though you said: she was demanded of them, and it was said: "Where are your children? And for what sin did you kill them?" All the interpretations are good and clear, except that (سُئلتْ) is the more common, so it is the dearest of them to me.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and his companions read it with shadda, and others of the people of Medina and elsewhere read it lightened. Both are correct. Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿صُحُفاً مُّنَشَّرَةً﴾, and this is evidence for whoever reads with shadda; and منشورة is [good] Arabic. The doubling and the lightening are [both possible] in it because of its multitude and because it is a plural, as you say: مررت بكباشٍ مذبّحةٍ and مذبوحةٍ (I passed by slaughtered rams). When it is singular, only the lightened form is permissible, as you say: رجل مقتول (a slain man), and you do not say مُقَتَّل.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ كُشِطَتْ﴾.
It was stripped off and folded up. In [129/a] the reading of ʿAbdullāh: "قشطت" with qāf; they are two dialectal forms. The Arabs say القافور and الكافور (camphor), and القَفّ and الكَفّ. When two letters are close in their point of articulation, they alternate in the dialects, as one says جدف and جدث (grave); fāʾ and thāʾ alternate in much of the language, as was said: الأثافي and الأثاثي [«الأثائى» in the source] (hearth-stones), and ثوب فُرْقبي and ثُرقبي (a kind of garment), and وقعوا في عاثور شرّ and عافور شرّ (they fell into a pit of evil).

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and his companions read it lightened, and the others with shadda.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّآ أَحْضَرَتْ ﴾.
It is the response (jawāb) to His saying: ﴿إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾ (1) and to what comes after it. ﴿وَإِذَا الْجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ﴾ (13): it was brought near.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلْخُنَّسِ﴾.
They are the five stars [planets] that recede (تخنس) in their course, then return, and تكنس: they hide, as gazelles hide (تكنس) in caves, which is the كِناس (lair). The five are: Bahrām [Mars], Zuḥal [Saturn], ʿUṭārid [Mercury], al-Zuhara [Venus] and al-Mushtarī [Jupiter].
Al-Kalbī said: al-Birjīs, meaning al-Mushtarī.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا عَسْعَسَ﴾.
The exegetes agreed that the meaning of "عسعس" is: it turned away. One of our companions used to claim that عسعس means: its beginning drew near and it grew dark. Abū al-Bilād the grammarian used to recite concerning it:
عَسْعَسَ حتى لو يشاءُ ادّنا * كان له من ضوئهِ مَقْبسُ
(It drew on [the night] until, if he wished, when he drew near, he would have a firebrand from its light.)
He means: إذ دنا (when he drew near); then he drops the hamza of إذ and assimilates the dhāl into the dāl. They used to consider this verse to be fabricated.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ﴾.
When the day rises high, that is the breathing of the morning.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَريمٍ﴾.
He means Gabriel, may Allah bless him and all the prophets.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى ٱلْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ﴾ [129/b].
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, who said: You read (بضنين), "with a miser", and we read (بظنين), "with one suspected". ʿĀṣim, the people of the Hijaz and Zayd ibn Thābit read (بضنين), and it is good. He says: the unseen of heaven comes to him, and he is begrudged in it (منفوس فيه), yet he does not withhold it from you. If in place of على there were عن, it would be acceptable, or the bāʾ, as you say: ما هو بضنين بالغيب (he is not miserly with the unseen). Those who said بظنين argued that على strengthens their view, as you say: ما أنت على فلان بمتهم (you are not suspected regarding So-and-so). And you say: ما هو على الغيب بظنين, i.e. not weak — He says: he is capable of bearing it. The Arabs say of a weak man or of a scanty thing: هو ظنون. I heard one of Quḍāʿa say: "The weak one (الظنون) may guide you to the right opinion", meaning the weak among men. If the meaning of ظنين is "weak", it is as was said: ماءٌ شريب and شروب (drinkable water), and قروني and قريني (my self/my resolve); and I heard: قروني and قريني, and قرونتي and قرينتي — except that the preferred way is not to add the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa]. And ناقة طعوم and طعيم, which is the one between lean and fat.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ﴾.
The Arabs say: إلى أين تذهب? (to where are you going?) and أين تذهب? (where are you going?). They say: ذهبت الشامَ (I went to Syria), ذهبت السوقَ (I went to the market), انطلقت الشامَ, انطلقت السوقَ, and خرجت الشامَ — we have heard it with these three words: خرجت, انطلقت and ذهبت. Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard the Arabs say: انطُلِقَ به الفورَ (he was taken off at once), putting it in the accusative on the sense of dropping the preposition (ilqāʾ al-ṣifa). One of Banū ʿUqayl recited to me:
تَصيحُ بنا حَنيفةُ إذ رأتنا * وأىّ الأرض تذهبُ للصِّياح
(Ḥanīfa shout at us when they see us — and to what land would you go at the shouting?)
He means: إلى أيّ الأرض تذهب (to which land would you go) [130/a]. They allowed dropping (إلى) with these words because they use them so much.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Takwīr
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿إذا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾: the meaning of ﴿كُوِّرَتْ﴾ is: its light was gathered together and wound up, as the turban is wound. One says «كُرْتُ العِمامَةَ عَلى رَأْسِي، أكُورُها» and «كَوَّرْتُها أُكَوِّرُها» when I wind it.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَإذا النُّجُومُ انْكَدَرَتْ﴾: «اِنْكَدَرَتْ» means they fell one after another and were scattered.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَإذا الجِبالُ سُيِّرَتْ﴾: they became a mirage.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَإذا العِشارُ عُطِّلَتْ﴾: «اَلْعِشارُ» are the pregnant she-camels that have their young in their bellies; the singular is «عُشَراءُ». They are called «عِشارٌ» only because when ten months have passed over her — and she gives birth, when she gives birth at full term, in a year — she is an عُشَراء, the finest she can be in pregnancy; and her owners do not neglect her except in the situation of the Resurrection. The Arabs were addressed with the matter of the ʿishār because their wealth and livelihood were mostly from camels.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
﴿وَإذا الوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ﴾: it was said: "The wild beasts will all be gathered, even the flies; they will be gathered for retaliation."
﴿وَإذا البِحارُ سُجِّرَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 6], with doubling, and it is also read «سُجِرَتْ» without doubling. As for the meaning of «سُجِّرَتْ», it was said that it is in the sense of «فُجِّرَتْ» (burst forth). It was also said: «سُجِّرَتْ» means filled; and from it is «اَلْبَحْرُ المَسْجُورُ», the filled sea. And it was said: the meaning of «سُجِّرَتْ» is: their waters were made into fires with which the people of the Fire are punished.

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿وَإذا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ﴾: every faction was paired with those it followed. It was also said: they were paired with their deeds; and it was said: the bodies were paired with the souls.

zajjaj:8-9.t:
﴿وَإذا المَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ﴾ ﴿بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾ — it is also read «وَإذا المَوْؤُودَةُ سَألَتْ بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ» ("and when the girl buried alive asks for what sin she was killed"). «اَلْمَوْؤُودَةُ» is the one whom the Arabs used to bury alive: when a daughter was born to one of them, he buried her alive. The meaning of her being asked "For what sin was she killed?!" is to reproach (tabkīt) her killer on the Day of Resurrection, because her answer is: "I was killed without any sin." Like this reproach is Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿يا عِيسى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ أأنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وأُمِّيَ إلَهَيْنِ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ قالَ سُبْحانَكَ ما يَكُونُ لِي أنْ أقُولَ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 116]: the question to him and his answer are only a reproach to those who claimed this about him. One says «وَأدْتُ، أئِدُ، وأْدًا» when I bury the newborn alive; the agent is «وائِدٌ», the feminine agent «وائِدَةٌ», and the feminine plural «وائِداتٌ». Al-Farazdaq said:
؎وَمِنّا الَّذِي مَنَعَ الوائِدا ∗∗∗ تِ فَأحْيا الوَئِيدَ ولَمْ يُوأدِ
(And among us is he who stopped the women who buried girls alive, so he gave life to the one to be buried, and she was not buried.)
Likewise, for whoever read «سَألَتْ بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ», her asking is a reproach to her killer.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَإذا الصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ﴾, and «نَشَرَتْ» (also read): the scrolls are spread open, and every person is given his book in his right hand or in his left, according to his deeds.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿وَإذا السَّماءُ كُشِطَتْ﴾ — it was also read «قُشِطَتْ» with qāf — and the meaning of both is "stripped off", as a roof is stripped off. One says «كَشَطْتُ السَّقْفَ» and «قَشَطْتُ السَّقْفَ» with one meaning. Qāf and kāf are frequently substituted one for the other; like that is «لَبَكْتُ الشَّيْءَ» and «لَبَقْتُهُ» when I mix it.

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿وَإذا الجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ﴾ and «سُعِرَتْ», with doubling and without; its meaning is "kindled", and likewise ﴿سُعِّرَتْ﴾, except that ﴿سُعِّرَتْ﴾ means "kindled time after time".

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿وَإذا الجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ﴾, that is: it was brought near to the God-fearing. The answer to these things is His saying: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما أحْضَرَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 14], that is: when these things which belong to the Day of Resurrection come about, at that time every soul will know what it has brought — that is, of deeds — and will be rewarded according to its deeds.

zajjaj:15-16.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالخُنَّسِ﴾ ﴿الجَوارِ الكُنَّسِ﴾: «اَلْخُنَّسُ» is the plural of «خانِسٌ», and «اَلْجَوارِي» is the plural of «جارِيَةٌ», from «جَرى، يَجْرِي» (to run). «اَلْخُنَّسُ» is the plural of «خانِسٌ» and «خانِسَةٌ», and likewise «اَلْكُنَّسُ» is the plural of «كانِسٌ» and «كانِسَةٌ». The meaning is "So I swear", and «لا» is emphatic. As for «اَلْخُنَّسُ» here, most of the exegesis says the stars are meant by it, because they recede (takhnis), that is, disappear, because the meaning of ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا عَسْعَسَ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 17] ﴿والصُّبْحِ إذا تَنَفَّسَ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 18]…
«[Translator's note: the sentence beginning "because the meaning of…" breaks off in the source without completion.]»
The meaning of «اَلْخُنَّسُ» and «اَلْكُنَّسُ» with regard to the stars is that they rise running, and likewise recede, that is, disappear, and likewise they «تَكْنُسُ»: they enter their lair (kinās), that is, they disappear in the places where they disappear. It was also said: «اَلْخُنَّسُ» here means the wild cows and the wild gazelles. «خُنَّسٌ» is the plural of «خانِسٌ»: gazelles are khunnas and cows are khunnas; «اَلْخَنْسُ» is shortness of the nose and its lying back from the mouth. If it refers to the cows or to the gazelles, then the meaning of «اَلْكُنَّسُ» is: those that «تَكْنُسُ», that is, enter the kinās, which is a branch of the branches of trees.

zajjaj:17-17.t: ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا عَسْعَسَ﴾: one says «عَسْعَسَ اللَّيْلُ» when the night approaches, and «عَسْعَسَ» when it departs. The two meanings come back to one thing, namely the beginning of darkness at its start and its departure at its end.

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿والصُّبْحِ إذا تَنَفَّسَ﴾: when it extends until it becomes clear daylight. The answer to the oath in these things — I mean ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالخُنَّسِ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 15] and what follows it — is His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 19], meaning that the Qur'an was brought down by Jibrīl, upon him be peace.

zajjaj:20-20.t: ﴿ذِي قُوَّةٍ عِنْدَ ذِي العَرْشِ مَكِينٍ﴾: it was said that part of the strength of Jibrīl ﷺ is that he overturned the city of the people of Lūṭ with the front feathers of his wing, and they were four towns.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
﴿وَما صاحِبُكم بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾: this too is an answer to the oath. The meaning is: "So I swear by these things that the Qur'an was brought down by Jibrīl, upon him be peace, and I swear by these things that your companion is not mad," meaning by it the Prophet ﷺ, because they said: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِي نُـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ إنَّكَ لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 6], so He said: ﴿ن والقَلَمِ وما يَسْطُرُونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 1] ﴿ما أنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾ [al-Qalam: 2], and He said in this place: ﴿وَما صاحِبُكم بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾.
﴿وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالأُفُقِ المُبِينِ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 23]: we have explained that in Sūrat al-Najm.

zajjaj:24-24.t: ﴿وَما هو عَلى الغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ﴾ — it is also read «بِظَنِينٍ». Whoever read «بِظَنِينٍ», its meaning is: he is not suspect regarding the unseen; he is trustworthy in what he conveyed from Allah, Majestic and Mighty. One says «ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا» in the sense of «اِتَّهَمْتُ زَيْدًا» ("I suspected Zayd"). Whoever read ﴿بِضَنِينٍ﴾, its meaning is: "he is not niggardly regarding the unseen", that is: he ﷺ conveys from Allah and teaches the Book of Allah.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿فَأيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ﴾: its meaning is: "So what road will you take that is clearer than this way which I have made clear to you?!"

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿لِمَن شاءَ مِنكم أنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ﴾, that is: uprightness is clear to you, so whoever wishes takes the road of truth and moderation, which is faith in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger. Then He informed them that the will regarding granting success (tawfīq) belongs to Him, and that they are not able to do that except by the will of Allah and His granting of success, saying: ﴿وَما تَشاءُونَ إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 29]. A further proof of that is: ﴿وَما تَوْفِيقِي إلا بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ﴾ [Hūd: 88]. This is a notification that man does no good except by Allah's granting of success, and no evil except by Allah's forsaking him, because good and evil are by His decree and His measuring: He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿اللَّهُ يَجْتَبِي إلَيْهِ مَن يَشاءُ ويَهْدِي إلَيْهِ مَن يُنِيبُ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 13].
